title: Portable release CPU profile
objective: Define and machine-check the portable release CPU breadth contract across GMP, FLINT, OpenBLAS, FFLAS, M4RI, igraph, and generated native compilation without changing the Linux glibc/libatomic baseline

oracles: Exact declarative profile and dependency build receipts

handoff.summary: Declared exact portable CPU baselines and dependency dispatch for Linux x64/arm64, macOS arm64, and Windows x64. Builders now derive GMP, OpenBLAS, FFLAS, M4RI, igraph, ff_poly, and smalljac policy from one fingerprinted authority; GMP configure choices are observed and reused only when valid; a release CLI validates the complete installed profile. The Apple Silicon observation parser was checked against the real M1 GMP config.log and reported host_cpu=aarch64 with path=arm64 generic.
risks: A full clean dependency rebuild was intentionally deferred to the integration/release builders; this lane validates builder declarations and synthetic complete receipts.

The isolated worktree's broad portable tier cannot run native integration cases without built FLINT/FFLAS artifacts; focused policy tests, architecture checks, strict Python, and the runner manifest pass.
This CPU profile is deliberately independent of the Linux glibc, libstdc++, and libatomic compatibility contract.
next_steps: Rebase or cherry-pick onto the shared release baseline and run clean Linux x64, macOS arm64, and Windows x64 dependency builds.
Invoke scripts/release-cpu-profile.cjs from each official native packager after dependencies are staged.
Retain clean-machine old-CPU execution and binary instruction inspection as independent release gates.
